name: table-cell
description: A single cell within a table-row of a queue table: text data, an icon/checkbox slot, a link, a dropdown/input field, or an action-button slot, depending on `type`. table-row composes several of these per row; header-block's divider marks the boundary between the header and the first row of cells.

props.name: type
props.description: Which cell kind this renders: checkbox-cell (was Penpot's "icon"), icon-cell (was "saved" and "action-icons", merged into one type that holds any number of icons), date, text-active-cell (was "title", "organisation" and "description", already identical), text-passive-cell (was "source"), text-subactive-cell (was "summary"), link, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, dropdown, input, empty-state, status-label, tag. See rationale.

props.name: content
props.description: The cell's text content, for text-bearing types (date, text-active-cell, text-passive-cell, text-subactive-cell, link, dropdown, input, tag). Not applicable to checkbox-cell, icon-cell, 1-action, 2-actions, 3-actions, or empty-state, which have fixed or composed content. For 1-action/2-actions/3-actions, doubles as the primary (rightmost) button's label.

props.name: tag_type
props.description: Only for type="tag": the tag's type (accent-1 | accent-2 | accent-3 | success | warning | danger | neutral), passed to the composed tag.

props.name: tag_subtype
props.description: Only for type="tag": active or passive, passed to the composed tag.

props.name: article
props.description: Only for type="link": der | die | das colors the link by grammatical gender (der keeps accent-1, die row-status-declined-text, das row-status-approved-text). Other values are ignored.

props.name: checkbox_role
props.description: Only meaningful when type="checkbox-cell". Unset (default): the normal row-select checkbox (unchecked / checked), toggled by table-row off the row's data-selected. "select-all": adds a third icon (checkbox-semi-select) and marks the cell data-checkbox-role="select-all", so table-row's select-all logic and table-cell's [data-state] rules can target it. Not sourced from the design.

props.name: editable
props.description: Text-bearing types only (not checkbox-cell/icon-cell/dropdown/input/1-action/2-actions/3-actions/empty-state/status-label). Renders a hidden .ds-input sibling alongside the text span and marks the cell data-editable so a same-row [data-edit-trigger] button (see extra_attrs) can toggle it into edit mode -- see component.js.

props.name: extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="1-action" (and as the primary button's attrs for "2-actions"/"3-actions"). Raw attribute string passed through to the composed text-button's own extra_attrs passthrough (see text-button/template.html) -- e.g. extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger' to wire an Edit button at a row's own editable cell, the same pattern popup already uses for data-popup-open/dismiss.

props.name: secondary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="2-actions"/"3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs, but for the secondary (middle, Dismiss-style) button instead of the primary one.

props.name: tertiary_label
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Label for the leftmost, lowest-emphasis of the 3 buttons (secondary priority, same as the middle button).

props.name: tertiary_extra_attrs
props.description: Only meaningful for type="3-actions". Same passthrough as extra_attrs/secondary_extra_attrs, but for the tertiary (leftmost) button.

props.name: options
props.description: Only meaningful when type="dropdown". A list of { value, label }: when given, the input-dropdown trigger is wired (data-dropdown-trigger) inside a .ds-dropdown wrapper with a dropdown-menu of these items, so the cell's dropdown actually opens (link components/dropdown-menu's component.js on the page). Omitted: the unwired trigger alone, unchanged.

props.name: dropdown_label
props.description: Only meaningful with options. The trigger's aria-label (the visible text is the current value, not what the control is for).

props.name: view_label
props.description: Text-bearing types only. Renders Figma's "Single-active-t+button" cell (D_SYSTEM node 28:949): the text clipped to one line with an ellipsis, followed by a secondary dotted text-button with this label (e.g. "view") that stays whole. The host page wires the button (e.g. to a popup showing the full text).

props.name: submit
props.description: Only for type "1-action": the action button is a submit button of the enclosing form.

rationale:
Layout (Figma flat table): every cell is one table row high -- spacing.row (44px) plus a 1px object-dark-passive hairline under it -- with spacing.cell (10px) padding, on bg.surface, and no vertical rules. Text is one line with an ellipsis; .ds-table-cell__clip clips an excerpt beside an inline "view" button. Cells share the row's width (flex 1 1 0%); fixed-content types (checkbox-cell, icon-cell, input, the action types, status-label) are flex: none and size to their content. Link cells right-align and never wrap (at most two lines, accent-1, underline on hover). Action cells left-align with a 16px right padding. A dropdown or input cell lets its field fill the cell; the input keeps its box border in the cell (Figma's table rows draw it), although input's transparent fill is borderless elsewhere.

Types: started as Penpot's 15 Type values and were merged where Penpot's own cells were identical. text-active-cell (was title / organisation / description -- pixel-identical in Penpot) is text.active body text; text-passive-cell (was source) and text-subactive-cell (was summary; body-text italic) keep Penpot's identifiers; icon-cell (was saved and action-icons) holds any number of icons, adopting action-icons' multi-icon layout, a deliberate deviation for a lone saved icon; checkbox-cell (was icon) is Penpot's generic single-icon cell, also used for the drag handle. Penpot's State axis is "Value 1" (an unused placeholder) on almost every type, so there is no `state` prop: hover lives in the composed controls. Composition, not restyling: action cells compose text-button, dropdown and input cells compose input-dropdown and input.

Icons: every glyph is the Figma D_SYSTEM set (node 103:4711) in icons/, inlined by component.js so currentColor and --_icon-fill / --_icon-mark apply. Checkbox and save rest as an input-icon outline on an input-fill box (input-icon rather than Figma's text-inactive, which disappears on the dark surface) and turn accent on hover; a selected checkbox is an accent box with an inverse mark; a saved bookmark fills with accent-2. checkbox-cell carries both an unchecked and a checked icon, and table-row's CSS swaps them off the row's data-selected, so selection needs no extra script. The checkbox styling is scoped to [data-icon="checkbox"], so a drag glyph in the same cell layout isn't recolored; data-icon="drag" paints Figma's drag glyph.

Row actions: in light, active action buttons rest in text-inactive (like an inactive tab title) and turn accent-1 while their row is hovered, focused or selected (Figma node 237:31166), so a long table isn't a wall of blue; disabled, loading, error and unread buttons keep their own color. Dark keeps them accent, because dark's text-inactive would not read on its background. 1-action, 2-actions and 3-actions share one shape (row, left-aligned, flex: none); 3-actions has no Penpot instance and follows 2-actions.

Additions not sourced from the design: `editable` renders the text and a hidden .ds-input side by side and toggles hidden, so the cell's size never changes between states; the trigger is a row's own button (extra_attrs='data-edit-trigger'), because editing sits behind an explicit action. extra_attrs / secondary_extra_attrs / tertiary_extra_attrs pass raw attributes through to the composed text-buttons (author markup, never user data). status-label is a plain, non-interactive span in system-success replacing an action group once a record is done -- not a disabled button, since there is nothing to click. `checkbox_role="select-all"` adds a third, semi-selected icon for a header checkbox that table-row drives. Shift+click on a Save icon saves or unsaves the range since the last Save click in the same table (visible rows, DOM order), dispatched as one ds-table-cell-favourite-toggle event with detail.range = true. Rendering verified in light and dark themes. Collapsed excerpt (explicit request 2026-10-11, threshold changed 2026-10-12): a text cell is an ellipsized excerpt (.ds-table-cell__clip) followed by a text button, usually "view". A button carrying data-collapse-label opts in: the excerpt is shown only when the column leaves room for as much text as "Dear Artist, This October, ARRIVAL Gallery will bring artists" in the excerpt's own font (the room is the cell's text box minus the button, the same in every row, so a column collapses entirely or not at all; re-measured on every width change and for cells added later). With less room component.js sets data-collapsed on the .ds-table-cell__text, style.css hides the excerpt, and the button is renamed after the field ("Summary", "Full Description") and lines up like a button standing in for column text. Other cells are untouched. The sample text is a constant in component.js because it is a behavior, not a style value.
a11y_notes: type="dropdown" renders a real .ds-input-dropdown <button> (listen for its ds-input-dropdown-open event); type="input" a real <input type="text">; type="link" a real <a href>. Icon cells use role="img" with an aria-label per icon, since each icon is its own unit; the inlined SVGs carry no separate text. Icons are fetched at runtime relative to the script's own URL (so they work wherever the system is vendored), and need http(s): from file:// the icon slots stay empty. Known gaps: the Save icon toggles on click but stays role="img" with no aria-pressed and no keyboard handler, so its state isn't announced and it is pointer-only, as is Shift+click range saving; `editable`'s switch to the input moves focus but isn't announced, and the input has no label. status-label is plain text. type="tag" is plain inline text (see tag): the label carries the meaning, color only reinforces it.
